It is suggested that the compressive damage process mainly obeys crack arresting and bridging mechanisms.
Alloy B doped with 1.5 at.% Sn exhibits about 2.1 % compressive ductility, while its fracture strength decreases by 126 MPa, compared to that of alloy A.

With Hf addition, the yield strength and fracture strength of alloy C increase respectively by 73 MPa and 166 MPa, and an increase of 4.2 % in ductility is observed (see Table 3), compared with those of alloy B.
It could be concluded that the Sn addition weakens the (Nb, Ti)ss, while the Hf addition strengthens the (Nb, Ti)ss and b(Nb, Ti)5Si3 at room temperature.
